title: SF5066 (2025-2026 Regular): Various judiciary, public safety and corrections policy provisions modifications and appropriation

other_topics: judicial-criminal-justice: Article 3, Sec. 5, 8, 9 (Minn. Stat. 609.185, 609.4752, 609.539) — first-degree murder, impersonating a public safety officer, theft of public funds
public-safety-approach: Article 3, Sec. 4 (Minn. Stat. 299A.956) — school safety grant program, plus Article 1-2 appropriations for judiciary, public safety and corrections

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2026-04-08; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2026/0/SF/5066/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced text as filed 2026-04-08; no votes recorded. Large omnibus (appropriations, school safety, emergency vehicles, new crimes, gun bills). Gun parts are Article 4 plus the gun-related repealer; quotes were chosen from the largest changes. Sec. 6 and 7 also redefine assault weapon and large-capacity magazine; Sec. 8-17 and 19-21 swap 'pistol or assault weapon' for 'pistol' in transfer-permit and background-check rules; Sec. 27 and 29 add ghost-gun and serialization rules; Sec. 30 strikes an under-21 assault weapon carry felony; Sec. 2 amends school-property carry. Sec. 1 strikes the 'Notwithstanding section 471.633' cross-reference and Sec. 32 repeals the local-regulation preemption sections 471.633, 471.634 and 624.717.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 471.635): A governmental subdivision may regulate by reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and nonarbitrary zoning ordinances, the location of businesses where firearms are sold by a firearms dealer.
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 609.666, subd. 2): A person who owns or possesses a firearm must secure the firearm when the firearm is not in the direct physical control or reach of the person as follows: (1) unloaded and equipped with a locking device; or (2) loaded or unloaded in a locked firearm storage unit.
Section 5 (Minn. Stat. 609.6672, subd. 2): A firearm industry member, by conduct unlawful in itself or unreasonable under all the circumstances, may not knowingly or recklessly create, maintain, or contribute to a public nuisance by selling, manufacturing, importing, or marketing a firearm-related product.
Section 18 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): An unlicensed person is prohibited from transferring a pistol to any other unlicensed person, unless: (1) the transfer is made through a firearms dealer as provided for in subdivision 3; or (2) the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 22 (Minn. Stat. 624.7139, subd. 1): A person who owns, possesses, or controls a firearm must report the loss or theft of the firearm to a law enforcement agency in the jurisdiction in which the loss or theft occurred as soon as practicable but not later than within 48 hours of the time the person knew or reasonably should have known of the loss or theft.
Section 25 (Minn. Stat. 624.7145, subd. 2): It is unlawful for a person to transfer, own, or possess semiautomatic military-style assault weapons.
Section 26 (Minn. Stat. 624.7146, subd. 2): It is unlawful for a person to manufacture, import, transfer, own, or possess large-capacity magazines.
Section 26 (Minn. Stat. 624.7146, subd. 4): A person who violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.
Section 28 (Minn. Stat. 624.7148, subd. 2): (a) A person who is not a federal firearms licensee is prohibited from assembling or manufacturing more than three firearms in a calendar year.
Section 31: Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 36, section 2, is revived and reenacted.
Section 32: Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 471.633; 471.634; 609.667; 609.67, subdivision 6; 624.7131, subdivision 12; 624.7132, subdivision 16; 624.714, subdivision 23; 624.717; and 624.7191, subdivision 4, are repealed.
